decision: Freeze candidate slate, not a winner; CAL selection occurs only after F3.1c metrics/threshold protocol is frozen.
PART_A weighted regularized logistic; PART_B LightGBM binary challenger; weighted empirical Bernoulli reference.
COUNT_A Negative-Binomial GLM on K-1; COUNT_B weighted conditional empirical PMF; zero process remains DG_PARTICIPATION.
CHAIN_A terminal-aware variable-order Markov/n-gram with explicit backoff; CHAIN_B regularized multinomial next-activity challenger.
TIME_A weighted conditional empirical temporal kernel; TIME_B quantile boosting challenger.
M2 arrival/duration fields represent planned temporal schedule quantities, not executed route travel-time truth; physical execution remains downstream.
DIST_A weighted conditional inverse-ECDF on raw wegkm; DIST_B quantile boosting challenger; expanded wegkm_imp stays sensitivity only.
LLM full-day schedule generation is excluded from core D_GEN v1 and reserved for a separately labelled experimental ablation.
Use F2.2 continuity rule: source_n < 30 => LOW_N; empirical/Markov cells must flag and deterministically back off, never silently pool.
P_GEW for person-day components; W_GEW for trip/transition components; weights never become features.
TRAIN fits candidates; CAL selects/tunes only under predeclared F3.1c protocol; TEST remains sealed.
More flexible challenger is promoted only by CAL evidence; complexity is not an acceptance criterion by itself.
Per-component deterministic seed namespaces plus canonical candidate ordering are mandatory.
No candidate may consume observed/chosen mode, route, feasible alternatives, execution outcomes or km_routing.
Concrete Python library/version choice is implementation metadata, not a scientific model-family decision.
Numeric candidate-promotion thresholds are not tuned or frozen in F3.1b.
